summary: Checks and updates a boundary marker byte stored one byte before a data block whose pointer lives at this+0x4. If the block pointer is non-null, reads the marker byte at data[-1]; if the marker is non-zero and not the 0xFF sentinel, runs boundary validation through sub_599560 with the value at this+0x8. After the check, unconditionally rewrites the marker byte at data[-1] to 0xFF (sentinel). Returns the prior marker value (with the return register's high bytes retaining pointer bits via the decompiler's LOBYTE aliasing).

operations.description: Load the data block pointer from this+0x4; if it is NULL, skip all marker processing.
Read the boundary marker byte at (data pointer - 1), the byte immediately preceding the block.
If the marker byte is non-zero and not the 0xFF sentinel, run boundary validation; an unset (0) or sentinel marker skips it.
sub_599560(value at this+0x8, 0) validates the buffer boundary; its byte result is captured into the return value.
Reload the data block pointer from this+0x4; only write the sentinel when it is non-NULL.
Write the 0xFF sentinel byte at (data pointer - 1), unconditionally re-arming the boundary marker.
Return the previous marker value (marker byte read at the start, or the sub_599560 validation result when that path ran).

unresolved: The object owning the data block at this+0x4 and the boundary-marker convention (a sentinel byte at block[-1]) is unidentified; owner is UnknownObject.
The return value mixes the prior marker byte with the sub_599560 result through LOBYTE aliasing of v2; the exact intended return register content is ambiguous.
The meaning of the 0 second argument to sub_599560 is unknown.
